newsitem.title: BERMUDA: RUGBY UNION - Winning All Blacks gaining more support.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Winning All Blacks gaining more support.

text.p: HAMILTON, June 27 - Like following a winning team? Who doesn't?
Waikato rugby fans are no different.
The All Blacks rolled into town yesterday and Hamilton and Waikato turned on a grand reception for them at Rugby Park.

Over 4000 fans laid aside their provincial feelings -- Waikato has only one All Black in reserve Scott McLeod -- and gave the winning All Blacks a warm greeting in their final training run before tomorrow's second test against the Pumas.
NZPA reports it was one of the biggest crowds the country's flagship sporting team has met at a training session.
Many of the All Blacks, who had assembled in Hamilton on Tuesday but held training runs slightly out of the main centre since, were pleasantly surprised at Rugby Park, sold out for the floodlit test.

They had been sceptical about the kind of support Waikato rugby fans would lend them. Most of the All Blacks had opposed the fans' favourite teams, Waikato and the Waikato Chiefs, in some tense national provincial championship, Ranfurly Shield and Super 12 battles.
But the generous support yesterday indicated that the All Blacks were still a passion for New Zealanders and the team were perhaps gathering more support with winning acts.
Although All Black coach John Hart spoke against night tests at this time of the year, he said they were glad to play in Hamilton.
Test lock Ian Jones took full part at yesterday's training, clearing any doubts about the bruised hips he had.

Hart said flanker Mark Carter suffered a hamstring strain on Wednesday while playing as a guest in Paeroa for Thames Valley. That deferred the selection of the reserves for the test from an expanded reserves squad.

Andrew Mehrtens, brought back into the squad after he suffered a hamstring problem against Fiji two weeks ago, will not be risked early which means the reserves will be Ofisa Tonu'u, Scott McLeod, Glen Osborne, Charles Riechelmann, Mark Allen and Norm Hewitt.
